#1314. Inzaghi to leave Al Hilal at the end of the season

Simone Inzaghi has decided to leave Al Hilal when his contract expires at the end of the season.

According to transfer expert Nicolò Schira, the former Inter and Lazio coach won’t extend his deal with the Saudi club. It runs until June and is worth a reported €26m a year.

Inzaghi moved to Riyadh in the summer of 2025, a few days after Inter lost the Champions League final. His time in Saudi Arabia has been a mix of success and frustration. He won the King’s Cup last season but missed out on the league title on the final day, when Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr took the crown.

Al Hilal also went 47 matches unbeaten under the Italian before NEOM ended the run in September.

His decision is sure to bring talk of a return to Serie A, where he won a Scudetto, two Coppa Italia titles and three Supercoppa Italiana trophies at Inter, and reached two Champions League finals. Reports in October suggested Juventus and Napoli could be options, along with interest from the Premier League.

First of all, between now (November) and then (June) there is a chasm, a whole realm of opportunities which can arise. Including ones from abroad (especially EPL, or the Bundesliga)

Furthermore, getting Inzaghi down from his high horse of €26m salary will not be easy, especially for the cash-strapped Serie A clubs anyway.

If he sincerely wishes to coach in Italy again, for Juventus (for example), then he must be ready for a paycut and learn to use strategy again, not just an unlimited transfer kitty.

sassuolo/udinese looks fit on him for the future.

#1313. Mauricio Pochettino Named Surprise Footballer as ‘Greatest Player’ He’s Seen

Former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager Mauricio Pochettino named the greatest footballer he's ever seen grace a pitch - and it's not Lionel Messi.

Pochettino has enjoyed an incredibly successful coaching career to date, overseeing two major Premier League clubs, as well as French giants Paris Saint-Germain. Currently in charge of the United States Men's National Team, the Argentine is being heavily linked with the Manchester United job, which is expected to be vacant soon as Michael Carrick prepares for his dismissal.

Naturally, having managed three of the biggest clubs in Europe, Pochettino has coached an array of talented footballers, including the likes of Messi, Kylian Mbappe, Neymar and Harry Kane.

However, he doesn't view any of these aforementioned stars as the best he's ever witnessed live.

Messi, Mbappe and Neymar might have been the figureheads of PSG's team under Pochettino, but the tactician has a soft spot for another player he managed at the Parc des Princes.

In an interview with Goal, Pochettino was quizzed on players he's worked with during his career. Asked to provide one-word phrases or responses to certain individuals, he heaped praise on Marco Verratti when the Italian's name was mentioned:

"The greatest players that I saw in my life."

Verratti now plies his trade in Qatar for Al Duhail, and is certainly past his best at 34. However, when he was under Pochettino's tutelage between 2021 and 2022, he was still at the peak of his powers.

Revered by those who worked with him, Verratti was indeed an outstanding multi-faceted midfielder who was excellent in every phase of the game. While it's well-documented that he had an unconventional lifestyle for a footballer, regularly enjoying partying and cigarettes which many believe held him back, he still managed to reach incredible heights with the Parisians.

Brazilian icon Neymar was asked to name five footballers he believes are even more technical than himself.

Devastating for the Italian himself and for PSG supporters, he narrowly missed out on the French giants' recent European dominance under Luis Enrique. The Ligue 1 outfit have won each of the last two Champions League titles, with the likes of Vitinha and Joao Neves guiding them to these triumphs — something Verratti was never able to do.

#1312. Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

#1311. Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave new era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

This was not as comfortable but still an impressive performance from this new and exciting team. Alysson, the Brazilian winger, was their man of the match.

Emery had warned his players of complacency against the Norwegian champions, but Villa took command from the start and were ahead after 23 minutes.

Ross Barkley scored twice against Fenerbahce last week and was in the right place again to head Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner past Arild Ostbo.

#1310. Football Manager 27: Release Date, Price & All You Need to Know

The Football Manager series is the most popular soccer management simulation games in the world, with developers Sports Interactive boasting a longstanding tradition of producing engaging new titles and growing a loyal fanbase in the process. Football Manager 27 is the latest title in the series and it is out in 2026, with plenty to get one's teeth into, including its complete list of playable leagues and licences.

For those unfamiliar with the series, Football Manager puts players in the role of a real-world football manager, giving them control over everything from transfers and tactics to team selection, training and press conferences. Rather than controlling individual players on the pitch like in other football games, the focus is on building a squad, developing a tactical system, explained in our beginner's guide to Football Manager tactics and formations, and making the key decisions needed to lead a club to glory.

Here, GIVEMESPORT brings you everything you need to know about the new FM27 game, including price, where to buy, features and more.

The official worldwide release date for Football Manager 27 is Tuesday November 10, 2026. Football Manager 27 Touch also launched on November 10 on Apple Arcade.

This closely follows the trend set by previous games, with Football Manager 26 having been released on 4 November 2025. FM 24 was also released in the first week of November 2023, with the prior edition releasing on 8 November 2022.

Fans were able to get their hands on the game early, through Launch Preview (previously known as Beta), which went live on October 29. That means fans will be playing FM 27 around two weeks in advance of the worldwide release.

What's more, there was a free-to-play period running for five days between October 29 and November 3.

Release date, key details and all you need to know about EA Sports FC 27

In the United Kingdom, Football Manager 27 costs £49.99, but some discounts are applied via certain retailers. Fans of the game based in the United States will have to pay $59.99 and Football Manager aficionados based in Europe will pay €59.99. This price is the same of the cost of FM26, which was also priced at £49.99 in the UK.

The game can be purchased via Steam, Epic Games, the Xbox PC app and Microsoft Store, as well as any major gaming retailer.

The hit TV show is coming to EA Sports FC's latest offering, here's how to play with Jason Sudeikis' character.

The most complete version of the game is typically released only on PC/Mac, with 3D animations and detailed gameplay requiring the processing power of a PC.

The console version of the game is only available on the Xbox Series X/S and the PlayStation 5, similar to FM26, which did not support play on older iterations of the consoles, like the Xbox One or the PS4.

FM27's Mobile edition is included with an active Netflix subscription and Football Manager 27 Touch will be playable on Apple Arcade from November 10.

To get you started on your journey to world domination in EA Sports FC 27, here are the best young players to buy in the game

One of the biggest developments in FM 27 comes in the form of game engine and matchday experience, with even more augmentations to the visual look and feel of the game, for those who value that aspect of playing.

The game interface has also been overhauled, with more streamlined tactical inputs available during matches and more dynamic data dashboards available so that you can further refine your approaches to games and player development.

Events such as cup draws and transfer deadline day have been restored to the game as a feature that players missed in previous iterations.

The world's most detailed football management game is set to release its latest edition in just a month's time and here is everything you need to know

Playtesting is one of the most important stages in development, and signals that the game is nearing release. During this period, a selection of fans are invited to play an early, in-development version of the game. Whilst playtesting allows fans to get a first taste of the new game and helps to build excitement around the release, the main focus is on gathering feedback from users, allowing them to highlight enjoyable new features of the game, whilst also reporting on bugs/glitches and areas that require minor tweaks.

In a community video, Chris Groves revealed that "members of the community have been visiting the studio regularly to test an in-development version of FM27", before going on to state that "over 40,000 [fans] registered interest" in the remote playtesting programme.

#1309. Inter target Calhanoglu renewal by Christmas but wage remains sticking point

Inter and Hakan Calhanoglu are working towards a contract renewal, but they still need to agree on wages before he can sign.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, via TuttoMercatoWeb, both sides want to continue together, and an agreement could be reached by Christmas if the terms fall into place. The 32-year-old’s current deal runs until June 2027 and pays him around €6.5m net per season.

The renewal talks follow a tense few months. During Inter’s pre-season tour of Australia in August, Calhanoglu said he was surprised there had been no talks over an extension. He insisted he was still attached to Milan, Inter and the fans, but said his future was in the club’s hands.

He was also reportedly worried that he was no longer seen as central to Inter’s plans, even though Cristian Chivu has backed him throughout and he remains key to the team.

The main obstacle is money. Calhanoglu wants a new two-year contract with the salary of a top player. Inter, meanwhile, want to reduce the fixed part of their wage bill, especially for a player of his age who has had recent fitness problems.

Talks are now open, and both sides will need to compromise to reach a deal.

#1308. 'I feel betrayed, misled, in shock. It was a stupid thing for them to do': ANDY WOODMAN relives the moment he was 'brutally' sacked by Bromley - and how his best mate Sir Gareth Southgate helped him cope

Published: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026

Every sacked manager has a sob story – but few dismissals have felt as harsh as Bromley’s recent decision to part ways with Andy Woodman.

In his first interview since that decision last month, the 55-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport about feelings of 'betrayal' and 'shock' before making his pitch to future employers. But the most eye-opening part of our candid conversation comes when I ask the man with more than four decades of experience to recall the Bromley Football Club he took over in 2021.

‘Look, Bromley is your classic non-League club,’ says Woodman. ‘I mean that with the greatest respect to all non-League clubs and I hate the word “non-League” as I think it should be “League Three”, as they are all professional.

‘But the facilities are non-League, the mentality is non-League. Everything is done day-to-day, hand-to-mouth, every penny counts, every decision that costs money counts, it is run by people’s personal money.

‘It was tough when I started: we had no turnstiles, no club shop, we trained on the pitch because it was astroturf, we had no gym.’

Under chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves, Woodman and Co, Bromley changed this mentality and shot up the pyramid, winning the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season.

Andy Woodman was sacked as Bromley boss last month despite leading the club to the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season

Woodman with the FA Trophy in 2022. 'Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair,' says the former Bromley boss

Pound for pound, no club has outperformed their history, budget and expectations in English football across the last decade as much as Bromley. But after an understandably tricky start in League One – two wins from their first 10 games – Woodman was sacked.

Asked how he feels about the decision, Woodman, who used to coach in the Arsenal academy system, says: ‘Yeah, I feel betrayed. Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair. That’s fine, I get how the football business works.

‘But the bit that didn't sit comfortably with me was the conversations I was having with people at the club or owners, everyone above me… there was no inkling of any of this. I feel misled. I was surprised.

‘One day, we were talking about plans and the way forward and how to get through this sticky little period with players out injured, then the next minute it was a change of direction. Nothing like, “Right, you’ve got three games to turn it round”, none of that, nothing.

‘My record was good there, the owner always said if anyone can churn out results it was myself. Football has no patience. In football, people always forget where they come from. I understand wanting to move forward. It’s disappointing really, that’s the best word I can use. I feel let down.

‘It was just a normal day when they told me. I was going into training, popped across to where the chairman’s office was and then was just told, “We are going to take a change of direction”. It was no more than that, I didn’t try to change the decision or ask why.

‘It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is… I am sure people will read this and think, “You deserve this” and “You deserve that” but what else can you do? There’s no easy way of doing it.

'When you have been told you are sacked, you don’t really want to stick around and have a long conversation. They didn’t give an explanation. They needed results, they said. We lost to Leicester which was not a great result, obviously. But realistically they are Leicester… and we are Bromley.’

'It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is'

Woodman, who used to be the Arsenal youth team goalkeeping coach, says: 'When I left Bromley that day, I just felt in shock to be really honest'

To hammer home that last point: Woodman’s first game was against Wealdstone in April 2021 in the National League at Hayes Lane. On that same weekend, Leicester were hosting soon-to-be champions Manchester City. Oh, and the Foxes won the FA Cup a month later.

‘When I left that day, I just felt in shock to be honest,’ continues Woodman. ‘I felt the next three games were winnable. I had played seven of the top 10 teams, beaten the top team Huddersfield, my goalie was just coming back from injury and some others were coming back.

‘We had two teams in the bottom four and one just outside so I felt it was my best opportunity to get some much-needed results.

‘To take someone out who has been in football 40 years and been in coaching 25 years and then to put (his former assistant) Byron Webster in charge who had just been fresh out of playing and has never done a coaching session… with every respect, it feels unfair to him. It was a stupid thing to do. I found that really strange, they took one point from those three games. It fascinates me.’

Now, with Bromley bottom of League One, Karl Robinson, the former Salford and MK Dons boss, has taken over. Woodman, though, is keen not to sound bitter and will remember his five-and-a-half years at the club with fondness. He says his best memories are taking Bromley into the Football League, playing at Newcastle in the FA Cup and beating ‘Hollywood Netflix club Wrexham’ in the FA Trophy final.

Sir Gareth Southgate remains his best friend, the pair having met as teenagers in the Crystal Palace academy. They took turns in being best man at each other’s wedding and Southgate is godfather of goalkeeper Andy’s son Freddie, who is on Liverpool’s books.

They also co-authored the 2004 book Woody and Nord which chronicles two polar opposite career paths that started at the same level, one going on to play (and later manage) England, the other a journeyman in the lower leagues.

‘Nothing surprises Gareth and I,’ adds Woodman. ‘We have been in the game for 40 years now. You can argue that in his tenure at England, he got them as high as they have ever been in 60 years and it still was not enough. So it doesn’t surprise us. People have to make decisions and they are business-related, only time will tell if it is the right decision but that’s not my problem any more.

Woodman and lifelong friend Sir Gareth Southgate at the release of their 2004 book 'Woody and Nord' which charts two very different careers in football

Southgate is godfather to Woodman's son Freddie, a goalkeeper on Liverpool's books

‘Gareth was very supportive, so was Alan Pardew and the support from the Premier League right down to the National League, there has been no end of messages I have had, which is comforting.

‘That first Saturday after being out, I didn’t want to be watching or listening to the game, I just wanted to get away because that is the worst. I have had two clubs ring me, there are ongoing conversations and I am just making sure it is the right vehicle for me. What I mean by that is I want an owner that is aligned and who thinks they can compete to get out of their league.

‘My record speaks for itself. If you ask most managers how many promotions and trophies they have won, I bet over long careers, they haven’t got many. For me, with the smallest budget in the leagues, we maximised the team and maximised success.

‘To get two promotions and an FA Trophy win against Wrexham, hitting the play-offs four times in five years, that is something I am really proud of. If nothing else, the Bromley supporters and town are grateful.’

#1307. Mauricio Pochettino Already Has His Own Dele Alli at Man Utd in Shea Lacey

Manchester United are set to sack Michael Carrick as manager, and Mauricio Pochettino is a leading contender to replace him in the dugout.

GIVEMESPORT sources understand the Argentine, who is currently the manager of the United States national team and signed a new contract until 2030 during the summer, has a release clause worth around $10m (£7.4m), and he is one of the top candidates to replace the iconic former midfielder.

United have won just one of their ten Premier League games this season and find themselves in 18th place following a dramatic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa prior to the international break, making a change of manager a necessity, despite Carrick only signing a two-year contract at the end of last season.

Pochettino is someone that has been looked at for several years at Manchester United as a potential manager. He was considered as an option to replace Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, but the club always opted for alternative options.

However, it now seems as though a deal could be done to bring the 54-year-old into Old Trafford. Pochettino is best known for his time at Tottenham, where he built a squad that reached the Champions League final and finished second in the Premier League.

The keys to that team was the foursome of Christian Eriksen, Heung-Min Son, Dele Alli, and Harry Kane, who were the most important cogs in the machine and regularly combined to win games for the team. The former PSG star is always keen to rebuild those relationships and find players wherever he goes who can take up that responsibility.

At PSG he had Messi, Neymar, and Mbappe. At Chelsea he had Cole Palmer and Nicolas Jackson working in tandem ahead of Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo. At Man Utd he has got an abundance of quality in attack, but there is one star who he could be ready to hand a big opportunity too in the starting lineup.

Carrick has so far preferred to use Amad, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko as his forward options, while Marcus Rashford featured heavily too before his recent hip issue. But in recent weeks, youngster Shea Lacey has been turning in some of the more impressive performances.

Against AS Roma he came off the bench to supply an assist as the team came from 2-0 down to win 3-2, and in his only start this season against Brighton in the EFL Cup he scored the opening goal. Now it's time for him to be unleashed more regularly, and Pochettino is the perfect coach for that to happen.

Lacey is one of the most talented young academy stars to come out of Carrington in recent years, and it's clear that he is now ready to make an impact in the Premier League and Champions League.

The number ten role is taken by Bruno Fernandes, but with Amad having not scored a goal for almost an entire calendar year and Benjamin Sesko sidelined until the new year with a shin injury, there is a huge chance for Lacey to step up.

Much like Dele was at Spurs, Lacey is young, hungry, and incredibly talented. He has the technical attributes to hang at the top level, has the eye for a killer pass, knows how to finish, and is more than capable of handling himself physically too.

Pochettino has a reputation for using young players and helping to develop them, and Lacey could be the perfect project for him. If their relationship becomes anything like the one Poch and Dele had, then this could be the start of something magical at Old Trafford.

#1306. Yildiz targets December return as Juventus plan comeback date

Kenan Yildiz is getting close to a return from injury, and Juventus are targeting next month’s game against Monza for his comeback.

According to Tuttosport, the 21-year-old will soon resume individual training at the Continassa. He’ll then gradually increase his workload, but he won’t be ready straight after the international break.

Juventus have been without their No 10 since August, a big blow that Luciano Spalletti has never used as an excuse. The player himself said he’ll be back “in December” while collecting the Bulgarelli Number 8 award in Bologna on Monday.

“I feel good and I hope to be playing again soon,” Yildiz said. “I miss Juventus so much. I miss the feeling of playing football.”

Fabio Capello, who presented the award, also had high praise for him, calling Yildiz “the Lamine Yamal of Italy”.

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Ice cold from Martinelli 🥶 https://t.co/uQEHb4x7eH

Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

#1304. Wayne Rooney’s I’m a Celebrity Fee Compared to Other Contestants

Former Manchester United striker Wayne Rooney is set to appear on the 2026 edition of 'I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here', and the pundit's eye-watering appearance fee has now been revealed.

The hit reality TV show kicks off next week, with the first episode set to air on Monday night on ITV. Fans of the cult classic, hosted by presenting duo Ant and Dec, are avidly awaiting this year's iteration, with football supporters particularly intrigued by how Rooney will fare in the jungle.

The legendary centre-forward, one of the best English footballers of all time, heads down under alongside a host of other stars from different fields, including the likes of Ricky Wilson, Leigh Francis and Chloe Burrows.

Arguably the biggest name in the show's initial group, it's no surprise that Rooney is set to earn substantially more than everyone else travelling to New South Wales next week.

Hanging up his boots in 2021, Rooney has already enjoyed a number of different ventures since retiring from football. He's overseen four separate clubs as a manager, including Derby County, Birmingham City and Plymouth Argyle, while he's also worked extensively as a pundit, mostly for BBC Sport.

His next adventure is now imminent, with the prolific goalscorer set to enter the world of reality TV at the start of next week.

Rooney's wife, Coleen, famously appeared on 'I'm a Celebrity' back in 2024, finishing second behind winner Danny Jones. The former footballer will be looking to go one better than his partner when he heads to Australia.

While his name speaks for itself, Rooney's reserved and down-to-earth persona has sparked huge amounts of interest from the public about how he might deal with the various obstacles that are thrown at contestants in the jungle.

For these reasons, the ex-number nine is set to take home a significant appearance fee, far more than any of the other starting participants.

From Gary Neville to Alex Scott to Mark Chapman, UK pundits are paid very handsomely for the roles of television and radio.

According to SuperTV247 on X, Rooney will be paid £800,000 for his presence on the reality show, a figure that will add to the Manchester United legend's net worth. This is £625,000 more than the next best-paid contestant, Kaiser Chiefs frontman Ricky Wilson.

Behind Rooney and the musician come presenter AJ Odudu, actress Joanna Page and comedian Leigh Francis, all on £150,000. Meanwhile, the lowest earner is set to be internet personality Jack Skipper, who will take home £50,000.

The eyeballs Rooney's antics in the jungle will bring to the show likely justified this enormous fee, although interestingly, Coleen earned a reported £1.5 million for her presence on the 2023 edition. This was on par with politician Nigel Farage's fee in 2023.

#1303. He Wants The Job: Conte is Man Utd's Only Better Option Than Pochettino

Manchester United are expected to sack manager Michael Carrick this week, according to GIVEMESPORT sources.

Following internal talks on Monday, Man United chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada are expected to recommend the dismissal of the 45-year-old to Sir Jim Ratcliffe in a meeting held in Monaco, GMS understands.

The Red Devils have produced two remarkable comebacks in the last week, coming from 2-0 down to beat AS Roma in the Champions League, and twice coming from two goals down to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Sunday.

However, the point against Unai Emery's men wasn't enough to take United out of the relegation zone, which shows how poor their season has been.

With 10 games played, they have registered just the one victory at home to newly-promoted Ipswich Town, and they could be bottom of the table by the time they kick off against Liverpool in their next match, should Crystal Palace beat Coventry City and Sunderland record at least a draw against Villa.

Wilcox and Berrada have clearly seen enough, having given Carrick a reprieve following the heavy defeats against Como and Bournemouth, and now it will be up to Ratcliffe to make the final decision.

With the expectation that he will leave, GMS revealed that United States manager Mauricio Pochettino is now a leading contender for the job if it becomes available.

The Argentine has barely been mentioned among the talk of possible Carrick replacements in recent weeks, but he has now emerged as a strong candidate, with $10m (around £7.5m) needed to activate the release clause in the contract he only signed in August.

The former Tottenham boss isn't the only manager admired, with appreciation at board level for two out-of-work managers in Eddie Howe, who they have held talks with according to Fabrizio Romano, and Julian Nagelsmann too.

Another manager currently available is Antonio Conte, and he is the only frontrunner for the job who would be a better appointment than Pochettino.

The one big concern with Conte is whether he has the patience to first build, and then stick around for, a project at a club, given what we have seen in the past.

However, if United are looking for a manager to make an immediate impact and who is a proven winner, then the Italian is the obvious choice, and he wants the job.

There is no doubt that the 57-year-old would send a much-needed rocket up some Red Devils stars who are performing nowhere near the levels they were in the second half of last season.

He should instantly gain the respect of the squad too, given he has won league titles at Chelsea, Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli.

Conte won those trophies in his first seasons in charge of Chelsea, Juventus and Napoli, proving that he knows how to be successful quickly.

Napoli had finished 10th the season before they won the Scudetto under the Italian manager, so he has shown that a big improvement is possible, as would be needed at Old Trafford if he took the reins now.

Conte can be volatile, but he has the passion and tactical nous to get results and change a team's fortunes, and he is the outstanding choice on the market for many reasons.

Pochettino has clearly shown he is a manager with a big personality who has held down huge jobs, but he doesn't have the proven success of winning trophies like Conte does.

Manchester United's potential starting eleven under Mauricio Pochettino has been predicted.

#1302. Calò breaks silence on Italy snub: ‘If I keep this up, I’ll deserve a call-up’

Giacomo Calò insists he’ll earn an Italy call-up if he keeps up his form for Frosinone, but he won’t add to the controversy over his omission from Roberto Mancini’s squad.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, via TuttoMercatoWeb, the midfielder spoke for the first time since being left out of the squad for this week’s Nations League games against France and Belgium. His agent, Vincenzo Pisacane, had already criticised Mancini and warned that the decision risked being “the death of meritocracy”, and the Italy coach responded on Monday.

“For now, Frosinone are my national team, and everything else comes later,” Calò said. “I don’t care much about the controversy, and I’d rather not fuel it. I know I’ll turn 30 in February and that carries weight. So far, the call-ups have always rewarded younger players.”

Calò has been one of the stories of the season. He has spent most of his career in Serie B and Serie C, but he has five goals in his first top-flight campaign, and no player in the division has created more chances.

Mancini picked teenagers Riccardo Cassano and Simone Lontani for the first time, but Calò doesn’t think his age should count against him.

“No, on the contrary, who cares if I’m 30? If I keep this up, I think I’ll deserve it. I let the pitch do the talking. Your performances tell you what you can become. I’m ambitious and I’m aiming high.

“Who’d have expected me to score five goals in Serie A and then be linked with the national team? Sometimes it still feels like I’m dreaming. In recent years I’ve always played between Serie B and Serie C, and I was a bit afraid of getting stuck in the lower leagues. I got out of there thanks to a positive environment like the one at Frosinone.

“I also think there’s been a bit of a lack of meritocracy towards me over the years. Today I’m a different player: more mature and ready.”

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

#1299. The 9 Players Ralf Rangnick Recommended to Manchester United

Rob is senior football editor at GiveMeSport, with over 15 years experience covering sport in various capacities since graduating from the University of Gloucestershire in 2008 with a degree in journalism. A childhood obsession for all things football developed into a career writing about the beautiful game, initially producing content for clients including Luton Town Football Club and the PGMOL. His first big interviews were with Premier League referees Howard Webb and Michael Oliver in 2009. He then spent four years producing written content for a betting website, mainly focusing on football, and was there to cover various games and tournaments including the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012. Rob joined GiveMeSport in 2013 (initially as a sub-editor before becoming a senior writer and then senior editor in 2020) and has covered countless football matches and other sporting events, interviewed various high-profile figures including Rio Ferdinand, Peter Crouch and Theo Walcott, and written well over 10,000 articles during that time. Rob has played a key role in GiveMeSport's coverage of the World Cups in 2014, 2018 and 2022, plus Euro 2016, Euro 2020 and Euro 2024, along with many Champions League finals. While football is Rob's area of expertise, he has also covered a wide range of other sports during his time at GiveMeSport including boxing, tennis and darts, as well as the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Olympic Games.

Not many Manchester United supporters will look back at Ralf Rangnick’s time at the helm fondly, though he did all he could to set the club up for a more prominent future. The 68-year-old German, who is currently in charge of the Austrian national team, was appointed the Red Devils’ manager on an interim basis in November 2021 - but ultimately failed to prove his worth.

He was poised to remain at the club in a consultancy role to support Erik ten Hag in his inaugural season in England, but upped and left soon after the Dutchman’s arrival. Rangnick, who has registered the worst points-per-game ratio of all managers to have attempted to steady the ship after Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement (with the exception of Ruben Amorim), took charge of all recruitment-based decisions at RB Leipzig and Red Bull Salzburg but failed to stamp his authority in Manchester in the same regard.

There were, however, a flurry of names that he recommended to the club during his short association, though none of them came to fruition. "Open-heart surgery" is what Rangnick claimed the squad needed during his final weeks at the club, as he made it clear that significant changes were required – and some time down the line, it’s evidently clear that the same issues are still embroiled at Old Trafford.

According to the Daily Mail, there were several names discussed as potential signings by Rangnick, including Manchester City duo Josko Gvardiol and Erling Haaland. But that’s not where the list ends. Some have made alternative high-profile moves, and some are still waiting to be snapped up. Let’s take a look at what they’re all up to now.

Enzo Fernandez is now playing for the blue half of Manchester after joining City from Chelsea for a joint-British record fee of £125 million in the summer.

The 25-year-old played a limited number of games for Benfica before making the move to England in 2023 and showed glimpses of his world-class qualities during his time at Stamford Bridge.

On the international stage, Fernandez was a key part of Lionel Scaloni’s 2022 World Cup-winning squad - even if it was Lionel Messi, one of the greatest football players of all time, who deservedly dominated the headlines during and after the tournament in Qatar. Even prior to that, though, United were reportedly keeping a close eye on the midfielder while he was at River Plate.

However, it's understood that the club were waiting for incoming manager Erik ten Hag to give the green light before signing him. The one (slight) silver lining is that his arrival may have stunted the development of England's Kobbie Mainoo, who has shown that he has the potential to become a top player for club and country - even if things didn't go to plan for him under Ruben Amorim.

United’s local rivals Manchester City are the Premier League club that took a calculated punt on the highly-rated defender. Despite his tender age, Josko Gvardiol starred for Croatia during the 2022 World Cup and rightfully earned praise and, in turn, his big-money move.

The 24-year-old was a domineering asset for his previous club, RB Leipzig, playing 87 games during his stint in Germany. After a shaky start to life in England, he has taken his game to new heights under the stewardship of Pep Guardiola. Given United's continued issues with Luke Shaw, a left-back of this quality going begging is one they may live to regret.

Despite playing second-fiddle to Erling Haaland during his Manchester City stint, Julian Alvarez is now widely regarded as one of the world's best forwards and deservedly so. He caught the eye of various top clubs while playing for River Plate in his native Argentina after notching 85 goal contributions in 122 games and transferred much of that form over to the Etihad Stadium.

Had United acted on Rangnick's advice, though, Alvarez might have been playing for the red side of Manchester instead. Rangnick was reportedly furious when the club failed to secure the Argentine's signature before he signed for City. After 36 goals in 103 appearances for the Sky Blues, he completed an £81 million switch to Atletico Madrid, where he managed to score an impressive 29 goals in his first season with the Spanish club.

Alvarez attempted to force a move to Barcelona in the summer but remains an Atletico player... for now.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Julian Alvarez became the first player in football history to win the Treble and the World Cup in the same season.

Luis Diaz's spell at Liverpool was largely positive, albeit marred ever-so-slightly by inconsistency at times. In his brightest moments, though, the livewire forward was truly electrifying. He haunted the Red Devils on numerous occasions as he has managed five goal contributions in six clashes, with a double coming during the Merseyside club's 3-0 victory at Old Trafford in September 2024. He made the move to Bayern Munich last summer and has hit the ground running in Germany.

Before becoming Jurgen Klopp’s marquee winter signing in 2022, the dynamic Colombian international was one of FC Porto’s driving forces, scoring 41 goals and registering 19 assists for the Portuguese heavyweights - so it’s no wonder that Rangnick had his eye on him. United's loss was undoubtedly Liverpool's gain, as he helped the Reds win a Premier League title.

Of all the missed opportunities, this one will sting the most for the Old Trafford faithful. Erling Haaland has been nothing short of extraordinary for Manchester City following his arrival from Borussia Dortmund. United legend Wayne Rooney even described him as the world's best footballer now that the Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo era has come to an end.

The goal-machine needed just 105 games to score his first 100 Premier League goals, and his links to Old Trafford go even further back than Rangnick's desperate plea. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer confirmed that the domineering forward was a man that the former United boss had told the club to sign long before he took the job in 2018.

As the 2021-22 season came to a close, it was patently clear that reinforcements in midfield were desperately needed at Old Trafford - hence why Konrad Laimer was eyed. At that time, the versatile midfielder had also caught the attention of Bayern Munich, who he eventually signed for, but Manchester United could have saved themselves money and hassle if they elected to sign him back when Rangnick first recommended the Austrian to the club’s higher-ups.

At Bayern, Laimer is a solid rotational option who would likely settle in well at Old Trafford, much like his former teammate Marcel Sabitzer did during his loan spell. Rangnick did at least get the chance to coach the midfielder, as he is a key part of the Austrian national team.

Alvaro Morata, 33, is somewhat of a footballing journeyman, having plied his trade for Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid, Juventus and Chelsea - though he has never quite managed to establish himself as one of Europe’s elite strikers. The Spaniard has scored goals wherever he's played during his career, although profligacy in some of the biggest fixtures has prevented him from establishing a reputation as a truly world-class forward.

The Spaniard was initially linked with a move to the Theatre of Dreams in 2017, but United opted for Romelu Lukaku instead. In the years since Rangnick's recommendation, the pressing-forward led Spain to European glory and sealed a move back to Italy, this time to multi-time Champions League winners, AC Milan. He quickly fell out of favour at the Serie A giants, though, and was shipped out on loan to Como at the beginning of the 2025/26 season.

Morata is now playing for Leganes, on loan from Como, in the second tier of Spanish football. File this one under 'bullet dodged', perhaps.

Christopher Nkunku could have become Manchester United’s first signing of the Ten Hag era after being one of RB Leipzig’s most notable stars. The Frenchman had a plethora of big-name clubs vying for his signature as he spearheaded Leipzig to a top-four finish in back-to-back seasons between 2021 and 2023, scoring a respectable total of 70 goals during his time at the club.

Injuries plagued the forward during his ill-fated spell with Chelsea, which left him determined to resurrect his career in Serie A. He scored eight goals in 35 games for Milan last season but is now back on loan with RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga.

Christopher Nkunku scored his third Premier League goal of the season as Chelsea beat Brighton at the Amex Stadium.

Imposing centre-forward Dusan Vlahovic, who was tipped to become a star on football's biggest stages, could have been a Manchester United player had the club been keen to listen more to Rangnick's transfer advice. Currently plying his trade in Turkey for Besiktas, the 26-year-old was previously one of Serie A's most recognisable forwards, despite struggling to show the same potency as he did during his time at Fiorentina.

Once on Arsenal's radar, there's still a chance that fans will get to see Vlahovic in the Premier League one day. But for now he's focused on scoring goals in the Turkish Super Lig.

All statistics courtesy of Transfermarkt - accurate as of 10/11/2026.

#1298. Mancini’s former teammate reveals: ‘He was unbearable at first, I locked him in a room’

Italy coach Roberto Mancini was “unbearable” when they first played together, according to Michele Serena, who says he once locked the Sampdoria star in a room until they sorted out their differences.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, via CalcioMercato, the former full-back looked back on a career that took him from Venezia to Juventus, Sampdoria, Fiorentina, Atlético Madrid, Parma and finally Inter, the club he supported as a boy. He joined Sampdoria from Juventus as part of the deal that took Gianluca Vialli to Turin.

“Roberto Mancini? Very good, but unbearable,” Serena said. “I argued with him in my first year, and Mantovani fined him and took my side. Vierchowod told me to apologise to Mancini, so after one training session I locked him in a small room with me until we finally sorted things out. After that, we built a good relationship, and we still speak today.”

Sinisa Mihajlović was another Sampdoria teammate, and he used to make Serena go in goal.

“After training, Mihajlović would put me in goal and take free-kicks. It would finish 20-0 or 20-1 to him.”

At Fiorentina, Serena played alongside Gabriel Batistuta and Rui Costa.

“Bati was the most complete No 9 I’ve ever seen. With Rui, we always wondered how he could smoke so many cigarettes and then run like that on the pitch.

“Edmundo? I’ll never forgive him for not coming back from the Rio Carnival. We had Batistuta out, and we were fighting for the Scudetto.”

Serena finished his career at Inter in 2003, but he’s still haunted by 5 May 2002. On the final day of that season, Héctor Cúper’s side lost 4-2 at Lazio, and Juventus took the title.

“I wanted to retire by winning the Scudetto with Inter, the team I’ve supported since I was a child. Instead, on that 5 May, I don’t know what happened… It’s a wound that’s still open, and it still hurts too much today.

“I was supposed to play that day instead of Gresko. I’d done everything to recover from an injury, but Cúper changed his mind at the last minute. I confronted him about it, because not playing that day really hurt me.”

#1297. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

🗣️ Commitment. Resilience. Teamwork. Michael's powerful message in full 👇 https://t.co/vWwJt1fW47

This was partly Carrick reasserting his own authority after a couple of weeks in which two senior players – defender Lisandro Martínez and captain Bruno Fernandes – decided to go public with their grievances and the team delivered a performance in the 4-1 hammering by Como that was up there with the very worst.

But a stony-faced Carrick was also sending a message to his squad to quit their public sniping and start pulling together for a wider cause. Moreover, to put the club and the team before yourself and your individual needs and complaints.

It was interesting that he used the word “entitlement”. His predecessor, Ruben Amorim, had uttered that same word to attack what he felt was an “entitlement culture” at the club and Carrick has evidently come to a similar conclusion.

We’ve spoken. There are always conversations going on. It’s pretty obvious how we’re all feeling. A reaction, a reaction from me.

The responsibility for me in this position is to lead. It is my responsibility, whatever goes on the pitch and what we look like, what we feel like.

Carrick had clearly thought hard about how he was going to tackle that today and what message he wanted to get across. The long and short of it was that the United manager was issuing a call to arms to his players to pull their finger out, respect the badge and start showing the kind of values of humility and hard work that the club is founded on. By name checking the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Matt Busby he was speaking about the people who exemplified the values United are all about

The foundations of this football club and values have been etched down for many years.

I totally understand and I get every single one of them. It comes down to being humble, to hard work and being really proud to live up to those values.

There is a resilience about this football club that has been shown for a long, long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, sustaining success, there is a resilience to this football club that runs very, very deep.

No definitive answer from Carrick, who says he wants to do what is best for the football club.

Definitely a change in communication strategy from Carrick, speaking from the heart rather than waiting for questions.

My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters and they can be proud of it with the identity that we show.

We have gone away from that just recently in certain games, which I’m fully aware of and definitely doing something about.

I think it’s important we all recognise that. I certainly recognise it. Our supporters of are the utmost importance to me and this football club.

For them to feel like they felt for five months at the start of the year and have that about us, that connection and that real vigour, intensity and enjoyment and passion is something we need to get back to.

Carrick says the dressing room is “not divided” but says it’s pretty clear the squad and everyone have to pull together and stop speaking out like has happened in public in response to questions about Martinez and Fernandes’ outbursts.

Principles are so important. We can win games, lose games, hopefully not but it can happen.

It’s how you do it and what it feels like is important for me. That the spirit and togetherness is there. It will be there. I’m working on solutions to move us forward.

He says loads of conversations have been going on. He says it’s his responsibility “to lead” and that “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and keep everyone else dry.”

Carrick adds on the Fernandes burglary. “It’s an awful thing to go through and we’re doing a lot of things to support him and his family.”

It was never about Ryan Giggs, it was never about Ryan Giggs, it was about Manchester United.

Wayne Rooney is top goalscorer of this football club. His biggest thing was playing for the team, sacrificing for the team and what was good for Manchester United.

Sir Alex Ferguson is the best manager of all-time. The greatest, for me. And working for him, his main priority was Manchester United.

Sir Matt [Busby] and Sir Bobby [Charlton], their resilience was beyond belief what they showed and how they rebuilt this football club. It was based on being humble, having humility and hard work. We can never lose that and I won’t let us lose that.

The Manchester United manager is under severe pressure after a run of no wins in seven games across all competitions, and senior players are talking out of school in post-game interviews.

Just when it appeared a line had been drawn under Lisandro Martinez taking on technical director Jason Wilcox, Bruno Fernandes reached for a petrol can and poured more fuel on the flames.

#1296. Football Manager 27 Wonderkids: Best Young Players to Buy in FM27

You've loaded up a new game on Football Manager 27 and you have a vision: build the best young team in the world and dominate for years. Unless you have one of the best academies in football, the only way you can do this is by recruiting as many wonderkids as possible.

A wonderkid is a young talent who possesses high potential and, with the right attitude, support and training, will evolve into a world-class player. You're looking for the next Cristiano Ronaldo or Lionel Messi, two of the greatest football players of all time. You're scouting for youth prospects who have what it takes to become the next big thing in football, whether that's in the mould of a swashbuckling centre-back such as Paolo Maldini, a formidable goalkeeper like Manuel Neuer or an all-action midfield dynamo akin to the Ballon d'Or-winning Rodri.

Here, GIVEMESPORT brings you the best wonderkid goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders and strikers, aged 20 and under, based on potential ability.

(Key: CA = Current Ability, PA = Potential Ability)

German duo Dennis Seimen and Florian Hellstern are the two best young goalkeepers in Football Manager 27, closely followed by Japanese prospect Rui Araki. Of that trio, Araki is the most affordable, and could mature into one of the best goalkeepers in the world if nurtured well by the right manager.

Dutch shotstopper Quenten Attigah has a very high ceiling, but may take some time to reach his potential given that he is only 17, but if you want to land a talented young netminder who can do a job straight away, you should consider scouting Pierce Charles.

Romario Cunha would be a decent signing for a team looking to climb divisions and would be affordable too, while Brazilian youngster Joao Pedro (not that one) is also a bargan at under £1 million.

To get you started on your journey to world domination in EA Sports FC 27, here are the best young players to buy in the game

It will come as little surprise to learn that Pau Cubarsi is top of the pile when it comes to wonderkid defenders in FM27 and he is virtually not for sale with Barcelona placing a mammoth valuation on his head. So it will take a lot of money and a lot of convincing to land his services in the game.

Brighton's centre-back Luka Vuskovic, one of the nominees for the 2026 Golden Boy award, is a more achievable target, but he will still command a hefty fee. If you're limited when it comes to budget, have a look at Inter Milan's Leondaro Bovio or Coventry City's Stephen Mfuni. If you're in the market for a left-back, do what you can to sign Saba Kharebashvili, who is primed to be one of the best left-backs in the world, according to FM's stats gurus.

Who will be taking Desire Doue's crown in 2026?

Lamine Yamal is the player with the highest potential in the game, and the best midfielder, but, much like his compatriot and team-mate Cubarsi, is practically unattainable, unless you're a manager who is capable of unsettling big-name stars and convincing them to join your crusade. Yamal is joined by the likes of Estevao and Yan Diomande, as well as Rio Ngumoha and Ayyoub Bouaddi, all among the best young players in world football, at the top of the list.

A little bit further down in terms of potential ability is Luca Williams-Barnett, who is more suited to an attacking role, while Mahdi Nicoli-Jazuli could morph into one of the best Number 10s in the game. Reggie Walsh, meanwhile, will be up there with Bouaddi as one of the best defensive midfielders around, should he reach his potential.

Aston Villa's imposing young striker Brian Madjo looks well placed to grow into the best out-and-out strikers in the game alongside Endrick, who has been a fixture of these lists for the past few years. It is worth looking to France and Italy for upcoming wonderkid strikers, with 16-year-old Montpellier prospect Lacine Megnan appearing particularly impressive. Roma have Antonio Arena in their ranks, while AC Milan's Francesco Camarda boasts similar potential.

If you are managing a club that is somewhat strapped for cash, here is a selection of the top wonderkids valued at £10 million or less.

The aforementioned Megnan features, but the best of the bunch looks to be Joshua Abe, Liverpool's exciting young winger. The United States is represented by Christopher Cupps and Gabriel Wesseh, both of whom would represent decent business.

Of course, in some cases, a loan move might be the only option, but there is satisfaction to be had in playing a part in a player's development. Indeed, if a young starlet has a positive experience at your club, who is to say they won't be inclined to stick around, or return at a later date?

Some of football's most exciting prospects can be found on FM 26.

#1295. Milan target 3 key signings in January transfer window

Milan plan to sign a centre-back, a left-back and a striker in January as they try to end the inconsistency that has held back their season.

According to Corriere dello Sport, Gerry Cardinale has repeatedly promised to strengthen Ruben Amorim’s squad for the second half of the campaign. Milan want to compete for the Scudetto and the Europa League, with the Coppa Italia still to come.

The Rossoneri have struggled whenever Amorim has rotated his squad. They’ve won only one of their midweek games this season, a 4-0 victory at Salzburg in which Cissè scored a hat-trick.

The rest have brought a 2-0 home defeat to Benfica, a 3-0 loss at Bournemouth, a 4-2 defeat to Bologna at San Siro after leading, and last week’s home loss to Ferencváros.

The club’s first new arrival won’t be a player. Markus Krösche will officially become Milan’s head of football on 1 January, but the former Eintracht Frankfurt director is already working for the club and could move to Milan early. His right-hand man Timmo Hardung could follow him from Frankfurt.

Their plan is clear: a new centre-back, a left-back and a striker to provide cover for Gonçalo Ramos.

#1294. USMNT fans in meltdown as head coach Mauricio Pochettino emerges as frontrunner for Manchester United job

By DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 21:47 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 23:51 EST, 9 November 2026

US soccer fans were sent into a frenzy on Monday by the news that Mauricio Pochettino is in pole position to join Manchester United.

As reported by the Daily Mail, Michael Carrick is facing the sack with United bosses leaning towards hiring a new coach during the international break.

Pochettino has emerged as a frontrunner for the role, despite signing a new contract following the World Cup, when he led the USMNT to the last 16.

The Argentine committed his future to the end of the next World Cup in 2030 but his contract includes a £7 million ($9.4 million) release clause. And news of Manchester United's interest left many USMNT fans fearing the worst.

'[That] was fun while it lasted!' one said. 'Wow - just when you thought things had settled a bit with the USMNT!' added a second, while a third said: 'Noooo they can’t have our coach!'

Many other supporters on social media refused to believe that Pochettino could leave but his future has been under the microscope ever since he took over in September 2024.

Mauricio Pochettino is in pole position to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United

Carrick is facing the sack with United leaning towards hiring a new coach in the coming weeks

The 54-year-old Pochettino has made no secret of his desire to return to the Premier League

The 54-year-old has made no secret of his desire to return to the Premier League, while it emerged ahead of the World Cup that he had held discussions with AC Milan.

Pochettino's team sparkled en route to the last 16, only to crash out against Belgium after President Trump's intervention over the red card shown to striker Folarin Balogun.

His initial contract expired after the tournament but after weeks of uncertainty, the former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton coach signed a four-year extension.

He is slated to take charge of a Nations League double-header against Haiti during this international break, with a press conference set for Friday.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, who were both under consideration when United gave Carrick more time to turn the season around following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last month, could also be in contention.
